title: Uniformizer charts for log smooth schemes over a trait
statement:
A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a Noetherian local domain $R$ of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal; a uniformizer $\pi$ is a generator of that ideal. The canonical log structure on $S$ is the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_S$ of sections invertible on the generic point of $S$, and $\pi$ gives its chart $\mathbf N\to R$, $1\mapsto\pi$. For a commutative monoid $P$ write $\mathbf Z[P]=\bigoplus_{p\in P}\mathbf Zz^p$ with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$.

Let $(V,M_V)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and let $(V,M_V)\to S$ be a morphism to a trait with its canonical log structure which is log smooth in the sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Let $\pi$ be a uniformizer of $R$. Then for every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$ there are an etale morphism $U\to V$ whose image contains the image of $\bar v$, a fine saturated monoid $P$ whose group completion $P^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free, an injective monoid homomorphism $u:\mathbf N\to P$, and a chart $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ of $M_V|_U$ in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], compatible through $u$ with the chart $1\mapsto\pi$ of $S$, such that the torsion subgroup of $\operatorname{Coker}(u^{\rm gp}:\mathbf Z\to P^{\rm gp})$ is finite of order invertible on $U$ and the induced scheme morphism $U\to S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], in particular smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 with Q=N (the uniformizer chart of the trait, footnote x), printed p.252, and Definition 3.6.1; it refines Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie (1988), Theorem 3.5 (WANTED locally), which identifies the chart notion of def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale with Kato's log smoothness.

proof.text: Fix $\bar v$. Keep the specified chart $Q=\mathbf N\to R$, $1\mapsto\pi$, of the canonical log structure; no etale change of the base trait is made. Here $Q$ is generated by $1$, embeds in $Q^{\rm gp}=\mathbf Z$, and is saturated since an integer with a positive multiple in $\mathbf N$ is nonnegative. Thus $Q$ is fs and its group completion is free of rank one. Apply [lem-per-log-smooth-differential-generators] to $f:(V,M_V)\to S$ and this chart. Put $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}$, $B=M_{V,\bar v}^{\rm gp}$, $D=A^\times$ and $C=B/D$. We obtain $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, $n\geq1$ invertible in $A$, and a logarithmic differential basis. The same lemma gives $C$ torsion-free, $D$ $n$-divisible, and finite cokernel killed by $n$ for $L=\mathbf Z^r\oplus\mathbf Z\to C$. These statements concern the quotient by units; they do not claim that the cokernel of $L\to B$ is finite.

source.place: XVI Definition 3.6.1 and Proposition 3.6.3 proof, first half, printed p.252.

proof.text: Define $\varphi:L\to B$ by sending the standard basis vectors of $\mathbf Z^r$ to the $t_i$ and the last $\mathbf Z=Q^{\rm gp}$ factor to the image of the base chart. The group $L=\mathbf Z^{r+1}$ is finite free. All hypotheses of [lem-per-divisible-unit-lattice-extension] hold by Step 1 with its subgroup $D=A^\times$. Obtain a finite free group $G$, an injection $i:L\to G$, and $h:G\to B$ extending $\varphi$, surjective onto $C$, with $G/i(L)$ killed by $n^a$ for some $a\geq0$. Fix these maps; the later chart will be constructed from them.

source.place: XVI Lemma 3.6.4, pp.252--253, used in the middle of Proposition 3.6.3.

proof.text: Set $P=h^{-1}(M_{V,\bar v})\subseteq G$. Apply [lem-per-kato-lattice-chart-realization] with exactly the basis from Step 1 and the maps from Step 2. Its log-smoothness and fixed-chart hypotheses are those of the item; $n$ is invertible in the geometric local ring, and the required finite-index condition and surjectivity are Step 2. It produces an fs monoid $P$ with $P^{\rm gp}=G$, a pointed etale neighbourhood $U\to V$, a chart with the prescribed germ $h|_P$, compatibility through $u(q)=i(0,q)$, and an etale comparison $U\to S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$. In particular the image of $U$ contains the image of $\bar v$. Since $G$ is free abelian, multiplication by any nonzero integer is injective in coordinates, so $P^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free. The injection of $L$ into $G$ restricts to an injection $\mathbf N\to P$ and also gives the injection on group completions.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, last paragraph, p.252.

proof.text: Write $K=G/i(0,\mathbf Z)$ additively. If $g\in G$ represents a torsion element of $K$, then $mg\in i(0,\mathbf Z)$ for some $m\geq1$. As $n^aG\subseteq i(L)$, write $n^ag=i(b,z)$ with $b\in\mathbf Z^r$. Then $i(mb,mz)=mn^ag\in i(0,\mathbf Z)$, so injectivity of $i$ gives $mb=0$, hence $b=0$. Therefore $n^a[g]=0$ in $K$. To see finiteness without a structure theorem, write $G=\mathbf Z^d$ using a free basis and let $w=i(0,1)\ne0$. The torsion classes are exactly the classes represented by $G\cap\mathbf Qw$. Choose a coordinate $w_j\ne0$. The map $tw\mapsto t$ identifies $(G\cap\mathbf Qw)/\mathbf Zw$ with a subgroup of $(\frac1{|w_j|}\mathbf Z)/\mathbf Z$, a finite cyclic group. The torsion subgroup is thus finite cyclic, say of order $e$; since killed by $n^a$, $e$ divides $n^a$. The chart-realization neighbourhood can be restricted to where $n$ is a unit: the inverse of the germ of $n$ in $A$ is represented on a pointed etale neighbourhood, and the equation $nb=1$ holds after refining by the defining stalk colimit. Restrict the chart and etale map to this neighbourhood. Because $n^a=ec$ for an integer $c$, the section $cn^{-a}$ is an inverse for $e$ there. Thus the torsion order is invertible on $U$. Finally an etale morphism is smooth by the last sentence of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. This proves every clause.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.6.3, p.252: finite invertible torsion; explicit lattice calculation and local restriction by the stalk definition.

proof_origin.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof and Lemma 3.6.4, printed pp.252--253, specialized to the chart of Definition 3.6.1; finite-cyclic torsion calculation written out.

lean.statement: theorem exists_uniformizer_chart (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R] (π : R) (hπ : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R = Ideal.span ({π} : Set R)) (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1) (S V : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (eS : S.scheme ≅ Spec (.of R)) (β : Multiplicative (ULift.{u} ℕ) →* S.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 S.scheme)))) (hβ : S.logStructure.IsChart (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 S.scheme)) β) (hβπ : ∀ n : Multiplicative (ULift.{u} ℕ), S.logStructure.alpha.app (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 S.scheme))) (β n) = eS.hom.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv (π ^ n.toAdd.down))) (f : EtaleLogHom V S) (hf : f.IsLogSmooth) : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (v : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ V.scheme), ∃ c : FSLogChart f, (Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField Ω V.scheme v).1 ∈ Set.range c.V.hom ∧ c.W = Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 S.scheme) ∧ (∃ e : c.P ≃* Multiplicative (ULift.{u} ℕ), HEq c.chartY (β.comp e.toMonoidHom)) ∧ Function.Injective c.g ∧ IsAddTorsionFree (Additive (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup c.Q)) ∧ Finite (CommGroup.torsion c.cokernel) ∧ (∀ x : c.V.left, IsUnit (Nat.card (CommGroup.torsion c.cokernel) : c.V.left.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ Etale c.comparison ∧ Smooth c.comparison
